data.description:
## Context
The OS/Python-invariant complexity-baseline lock currently runs inside every test-matrix cell in `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml`: Ubuntu costs 52/54/55s and macOS costs 45s. The same commit has already been checked out in the single Ubuntu lint job. Running the policy there once preserves the gate while eliminating four duplicate invocations and their fetch/merge-base work, estimated at about 154 net runner-seconds per Verified run. CPython and Django use dedicated single lint jobs; Rust and Kubernetes use dedicated tidy/verify surfaces. No rejection was found; `humble-cinnamoned-mussel` fixed lock correctness but did not require matrix duplication.

## Plan
- Strengthen workflow policy tests to require exactly one complexity-lock invocation, in the single lint job, and to prohibit it in the OS/Python test matrix.
- Move the existing unchanged script invocation and definition-vs-tree guard from `jobs.test` to `jobs.lint`.
- Run held-out RED→GREEN, a duplicate-invocation mutation, workflow/config tests, repository gates, and compare CI job timing after Gerrit upload. Back-out is a Gerrit revert.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --lock` executes exactly once for a Verified change.
- [ ] The invocation is a blocking step in the single lint job and is absent from the test matrix.
- [ ] The existing fail-closed and definition-vs-tree-skew behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] A workflow unit oracle fails on the current four-matrix-invocation placement and on any future duplicate placement.
- [ ] Reintroducing the matrix invocation returns the held-out oracle to RED.
- [ ] CI evidence quantifies runner-seconds saved without adding jobs, runners, or reducing policy coverage.
- [ ] Focused tests, lint, typecheck, Gerrit LLM-Review +1, and Gerrit Verified +1 pass before merge.
- [ ] The final ticket comment records RED/GREEN/mutation evidence and measured savings.
data.title: Run complexity baseline lock once per Verified change
